judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures hold against the artifacts. verify.json carries exactly one entry per id, every non-manual one of type 'solve', and each cited problem prints strictly more than the scalar that entry checks. Problem 1: '(a) Name the statement that permits AB + BC = AC, and say whether it is a definition, a postulate or a theorem. (b) Solve for x' -- id 1 is solve '(2*x+3)+(3*x-1)-27' -> [5], covering (b) only. Problem 3: '(a) Name the postulate that lets you add the two smaller measures' -- id 3 -> [13], (a) uncovered. Problem 6: '(a) Write the converse ... (b) Solve for x and find both measures. (c) Explain how this pair settles the truth of the converse' -- id 6 -> [15]; neither the converse, nor the explanation, nor the two 67-degree measures the key boxes are recorded. Problem 4 asks for the converse and the counterexample decision and records only the solution set [-6, 6]; problem 5 asks for the two packed conditionals and the validity explanation and records only [8]; problem 8 asks for PA and PB (both 19) and for which half of the biconditional was used, and records only [6]. Nothing but the terminal scalar is in the file, and none of the six carries a companion manual entry, so the gate chain reports the sheet fully verified. One correction to the judge's wording rather than its substance: problem 6 asks for a converse and an explanation, not for a named postulate or theorem, so grouping it with 1 and 3 is loose -- but the coverage gap in problem 6 is real and larger than in either of them. Independent recomputation agrees with the key everywhere: 5, 13, -6 and 6, 8, 15 (giving 67 and 67), 6 (giving PA = PB = 19). REJECT is correct.

strengths_to_preserve: The algebraic-converse device in problems 4 and 6 is the best thing on this sheet and should be reused. 'Is the converse true?' is turned into 'solve completely and look at the solution set', so the counterexample x = -6 falls out of the algebra instead of being asserted; problem 6 then runs the identical move geometrically, using two congruent-but-adjacent 67-degree angles to kill the converse of the Vertical Angles Theorem. The same reasoning shape appears twice in two different representations.

Problem 8 part (c) -- 'Which half of the biconditional did you use, the half starting from equal distances, or the half starting from the bisector?' -- is a discriminator almost no sheet on this topic asks. It is the difference between memorising 'perpendicular bisector means equidistant' and knowing that a biconditional is two separately usable implications.

Every manual item in the answer key carries an explicit grading note, not just a model answer. Problem 2's reads 'accept "definition" or "postulate" on the midpoint row only when the reason given is that no proof is involved. The reason column carries the learning here, not the label.' A parent who is not a geometry specialist can mark that.

The study guide's section 2 (classification) marks its own worked example AND its try-it as manual -- 'Classification is read by a person, not computed -- flagged for manual review' -- rather than inventing a computable stand-in. That is the honest encoding, and it is the encoding the worksheet's mixed items failed to reach for.

root_causes.description: Coverage is contracted per PROBLEM ID, not per printed RESPONSE SLOT. SKILL.md line 189 states that verification 'hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check (use `manual` for the unverifiable ones), so a partially-verified answer key can never slip through'. On a sheet where six of ten problems print two or three lettered responses, one scalar entry discharges the whole problem and the remaining slots are invisible to every gate.
evidence: verify.json: ten entries, one per id; ids 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 are single 'solve' entries with a scalar or scalar-list expected
worksheet.pdf problem 1 prints (a) and (b); problem 4, 5, 6 and 8 each print (a), (b) and (c)
SKILL.md line 189: 'every problem id 1..N has at least one check'
gate_log.txt gate summary shows verify-ws MANUAL and every other gate PASS -- no gate observes the uncovered slots

root_causes.description: SKILL.md line 257 already says 'Use `manual` for ... any explanation/reasoning answer', but it is written as advice about whole problems. Nothing tells the author what to do with a MIXED item -- one that prints both a computable value and an explanation. The author read the rule as 'this problem has a value, so it is not a manual problem' and dropped the explanation slot entirely, which is exactly what happened on problems 4, 5, 6 and 8.
evidence: SKILL.md line 257: 'Use `manual` for: graph sketches, sign charts, word problem setups, two-column proofs, constructions, ... and any explanation/reasoning answer.'
verify.json ids 2, 7, 9, 10 are manual and are the four problems with NO computable value; ids 4, 5, 6, 8 all have both a value and an explanation and are recorded as machine-verified only

final_response.md asserts 'Six of the ten problems were machine-verified with SymPy (1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8); every boxed value in the key was bound back to the recomputed answer' -- true of the boxed values, false of the printed responses

improvements.title: Require one verification entry per printed response slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Change the coverage rule from 'one check per problem id' to 'one check per printed response slot'. (a) Rewrite the SKILL.md line-189 sentence to require an entry for every lettered part, blank, box or \ansblank an item prints, using a `manual` entry where the slot is prose. (b) Extend tests/check_layout.py to count response slots inside each \problem segment -- lettered parts introduced by (a)/(b)/(c), \ansblank, \answerline and \underline runs -- and exit non-zero when that count exceeds the number of verify entries carrying that id. The schema already supports several entries per id and other cases in this same shard use it (curr-306 id 2, curr-313 id 5), so this needs no schema change. For curr-302 specifically it adds: an eval for problem 6's two 67-degree measures, two evals for problem 8's PA and PB (both 19), and manual companions for the naming and explanation parts of 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8.
improvements.regression_test: Add a fixture worksheet whose problem 1 prints parts (a), (b) and (c) with a verify JSON carrying a single solve entry for id 1, and assert check_layout.py exits non-zero naming problem 1 and the slot count. It exits 0 today, which is the defect.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the dominant hard failure across this shard. On curr-302 it converts six 'fully verified' problems into six problems whose verification actually matches what the student writes, and it recovers four machine-checkable values (67, 67, 19, 19) that are printed in the key with no check behind them.
improvements.risk: Medium. A naive slot counter will fire on decorative underlines and on sheets that print both an inline blank and a trailing 'Answer:' line. Land it warn-only for one run, tune against the existing eval corpus, then promote to a hard gate.

improvements.title: A problem that also asks for a name, a converse or an explanation needs a companion manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: State in SKILL.md that `manual` is a property of a RESPONSE, not of a problem, and that any item printing both a computable value and an explanation must carry both entry kinds under the same id. Add a lint to scripts/verify.py that scans the worksheet .tex segment for each id for imperative prose markers ('name the', 'explain', 'justify', 'state why', 'write the converse', 'say whether', 'which half') and exits 2 with a named list when the id has no `manual` entry. Exit 2 is the right severity -- it is already the manual-review channel and build.sh already reports it.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem 2 prose reads 'Name the postulate that permits this step, then solve for x' with a verify JSON holding only a solve entry for id 2; assert verify.py exits 2 and its stderr names problem 2. Today it exits 0 for that problem.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the false 'fully machine-verified' claim from every sheet in this shard that mixes computation with justification, and makes the manual boundary in final_response.md accurate rather than optimistic.
improvements.risk: Low-to-medium. Keyword scanning will produce false positives on stems that use 'explain' inside a scenario rather than as an instruction. Because the consequence is exit 2 and a printed list rather than a build failure, a false positive costs the author one line of review, not a rebuild.

case_summary: The geometry logic is sound and the sheet is genuinely well designed: the algebraic-converse device carries the whole topic, problem 8 asks the sharpest available question about biconditionals, and every one of the four honest manual items has a real grading note. Every value recomputes (5, 13, -6/6, 8, 15, 6). The rejection is this shard's dominant defect in a mixed-item form: six problems print two or three lettered responses each -- name the postulate, write the converse, give both measures, say which half of the biconditional -- and verify.json holds exactly one scalar entry per id, with no manual companion. Four honest manual entries on the pure-reasoning problems prove the mechanism was understood; it simply was not applied where a problem had both a number and an argument. Two machine-checkable values are also collateral casualties: problem 6's two 67-degree measures and problem 8's PA = PB = 19 are boxed in the key and appear in no check.
